translations.title: Vaginal Tablet for Candidal Vaginitis
translations.efficacy: This medicine is used for candidal vaginitis.
translations.usage: Adults insert one tablet (100 mg) deep into the vagina once a day at bedtime for 6 consecutive days. For short-course treatment, adults insert 2 tablets (200 mg) deep into the vagina once a day at bedtime for 3 consecutive days.
translations.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it. Before using this medicine, talk to a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breastfeeding. Do not use it during menstruation. While using it, do not use tampons, vaginal douches, cleansers or other products inserted into the vagina. It is better to avoid vaginal intercourse while using it, as a partner may be infected during intercourse.

translations.title: Lidocaine Cream for Reduced Sensitivity of the Male Genitals
translations.efficacy: This medicine is used to reduce the sensitivity of touch of the male genitals.
translations.usage: Apply 0.25-0.66 g of the cream (23-62 mg as lidocaine) to the affected area 5-15 minutes before intercourse. The amount and the application time differ from person to person, so use the smallest effective amount, and do not apply more than 2 g (184 mg as lidocaine) within 24 hours.
translations.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or to other amide-type local anaesthetics, if the application site has a wound or inflammation, or if your partner is pregnant. Before using this medicine, talk to a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver or kidney disease or are hypersensitive to propylene glycol. For external use only. Do not use it in the eyes or the nose. It is better not to apply it repeatedly to the same area.

translations.title: Antiviral Cream for Herpes Simplex Virus Infections
translations.efficacy: This medicine is used for herpes simplex virus infections, including initial and recurrent genital herpes and cold sores.
translations.usage: Apply it to the affected area 5 times a day at intervals of about 4 hours. Continue the treatment for 5 days; if it has not healed after 5 days of use, it may be used for a further 5 days.
translations.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you are breastfeeding, or in children. Before using this medicine, talk to a doctor or pharmacist if you have an immune deficiency such as AIDS or a bone marrow transplant, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant. Start the treatment as early as possible; for a recurrence, start it when the first warning symptoms or lesions appear. Follow the directions and the amount exactly. Do not use it to prevent transmission to others or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex infection. Do not use it as a base to dilute this medicine or to mix other medicines. This medicine is for external use only.

translations.efficacy: This medicine is used for wounds and scars from hypertrophic and keloid, movement-restricting or cosmetic skin damage after surgery, amputation, burns or accidents, and for traumatic contracture and cicatricial stricture.

summaryTable.How it works: Blocks the multiplication of the herpes simplex virus
summaryTable.Main use: Initial and recurrent genital herpes; cold sores
summaryTable.Who should be careful: Breastfeeding; children; immune deficiency; hypersensitivity to propylene glycol
summaryTable.Choosing point: Products with the same generic code (102935CCM) have the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

translations.title: Cream for Temporary Relief of Haemorrhoid Discomfort
translations.efficacy: This medicine is used for the temporary relief of discomfort, burning and itching caused by haemorrhoids.
translations.usage: Adults apply it directly to the affected area up to 3 times a day.
translations.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it. Use it with care if you are hypersensitive to propylene glycol or have had an allergic reaction to it. Before using this medicine, talk to a doctor or pharmacist for children aged 12 years or under and if you are pregnant or may be pregnant. Follow the directions and the amount exactly. When giving it to a child, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine is for use on the anal area only; do not use it in the eyes.

summaryTable.How it works: Relieves discomfort, burning and itching around the anus
summaryTable.Main use: Temporary relief of haemorrhoid symptoms
summaryTable.Who should be careful: Children aged 12 years or under; pregnancy; hypersensitivity to propylene glycol
summaryTable.Choosing point: Products with the same generic code (392430CCM) have the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

translations.title: Cream for Itching, Insect Bites and Contact Dermatitis
translations.efficacy: This medicine is used for itching, insect bites, urticaria, prickly heat, contact dermatitis caused by lacquer and similar, chilblains, eczema, dermatitis and skin erosion.
translations.usage: Apply it to the affected area once to several times a day.
translations.caution: Do not use this medicine on areas affected by chickenpox, athlete's foot, tinea or similar, or on areas with pus. Before using this medicine, talk to a doctor or pharmacist if you are hypersensitive to medicines or cosmetics, if you have an allergic constitution, if the skin is very moist or eroded, or if the affected area is extensive. Follow the directions and the amount exactly. When giving it to a child, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. If there is no improvement after using it for 5 to 6 days, stop using it and talk to a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Relieves itching and inflammation of the skin
summaryTable.Main use: Itching, insect bites, urticaria, prickly heat, contact dermatitis, chilblains, eczema
summaryTable.Who should be careful: Chickenpox, athlete's foot, tinea or areas with pus; extensive affected areas
summaryTable.Choosing point: Products with the same generic code (B23200CCM) have the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

translations.title: Cream for Eczema, Dermatitis and Insect Bites
translations.efficacy: This medicine is used for eczema, dermatitis, prickly heat, dermatitis caused by lacquer and similar, itching, insect bites, urticaria and chilblains.
translations.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times a day.
translations.caution: Do not use this medicine in infants aged 30 months or under, in or around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on eczema, on wounds or on sensitive skin. In particular, do not use a large amount on peeling skin or on areas with blisters. Before using this medicine, talk to a doctor or pharmacist if you have had an allergic reaction to a medicine or a cosmetic (rash, redness, itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer and similar), if you have an allergic constitution, if the skin is very moist, eroded or severely inflamed, or for children. If there is no improvement after using it for 5 to 6 days, stop using it and talk to a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Relieves itching and inflammation of the skin
summaryTable.Main use: Eczema, dermatitis, prickly heat, itching, insect bites, urticaria, chilblains
summaryTable.Who should be careful: Infants aged 30 months or under; eyes, mucous membranes, wounds and sensitive skin must be avoided
summaryTable.Choosing point: Products with the same generic code (A57300CCM) have the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

translations.title: Cream for Scars and Skin Damage after Surgery, Burns or Accidents
translations.efficacy: This medicine is used for wounds and scars from hypertrophic and keloid, movement-restricting or cosmetic skin damage after surgery, amputation, burns or accidents, and for traumatic contracture and cicatricial stricture.
translations.usage: Massage it gently into the wound area several times a day until it is fully absorbed. For a severe wound or an old scar, fix it in place with a dressing and leave it overnight.
translations.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you are pregnant, or on an incised or unhealed wound or on a wound area on mucosal skin that is weeping. Before using this medicine, talk to a doctor or pharmacist if you are breastfeeding. When giving it to a child, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Take care that the wound is not exposed to the heat of the sun or to light, and for a fresh wound avoid physical stimulation such as extreme cold, ultraviolet light or strong massage.

summaryTable.How it works: Softens and improves the appearance of scars and damaged skin
summaryTable.Main use: Hypertrophic and keloid scars, traumatic contracture, cicatricial stricture
summaryTable.Who should be careful: Pregnancy; incised or unhealed wounds; weeping wounds on mucosal skin
summaryTable.Choosing point: Products with the same generic code (A18500CCM) have the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

translations.title: Ointment for Corticosteroid-Responsive Skin Disorders with Secondary Infection
translations.efficacy: This medicine is used for the initial treatment of corticosteroid-responsive skin disorders secondarily infected by neomycin-sensitive bacteria (dermatitis, infected wounds).
translations.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day.
translations.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to this medicine or to aminoglycoside antibiotics such as streptomycin, kanamycin, gentamicin or neomycin, or to bacitracin; if you have a skin infection (skin tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, tinea, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum; an ulcer (except Behcet's disease); a deep second-degree or worse burn or frostbite; perioral dermatitis; acne vulgaris; rosacea; or a wound in or around the eyes or on the breast area.

summaryTable.How it works: Relieves inflammation and treats secondary bacterial infection of the skin
summaryTable.Main use: Dermatitis and infected wounds responsive to corticosteroids
summaryTable.Who should be careful: Hypersensitivity to aminoglycosides or bacitracin; skin infections; wounds around the eyes or on the breast
summaryTable.Choosing point: Products with the same generic code (346500COM) have the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.
